headline: A 2021 law requires federal agencies to post their budget justification materials online within two weeks of sending them to Congress.
what_it_does: Federal agencies must post their budget justification materials on a single searchable government website, such as USAspending.gov, and on their own websites. The materials must be in an open format that lets people download individual reports, all reports at once, or search results. The Office of Management and Budget must also run a public website that lists which agencies submit these materials, the submission and posting dates, and links to the materials.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that submit budget justification materials to Congress
who_it_affects.how: They must post those materials online in an open, searchable format no later than two weeks after sending them to Congress.

who_it_affects.group: The Office of Management and Budget
who_it_affects.how: It must maintain a public website that tracks which agencies submit materials, when they were submitted and posted, and where to find them.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the public, journalists, and researchers who follow federal spending
who_it_affects.how: They can find and download agency budget justification materials in one place instead of requesting them separately.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on September 24, 2021, and the summary does not list a separate later effective date.
